memory_candidates.content: In bash scripts using `set -euo pipefail`, a counter function like `log_warn() { ((warnings++)); }` is a landmine: bare post-increment `((var++))` evaluates to the PRE-increment value, so the very first 0-to-1 increment anywhere in the script's lifetime is arithmetic false and aborts the whole script under -e, silently truncating output before any later summary/exit logic runs. Always use the assignment form `var=$((var + 1))` for counters in scripts that set -e; it has no such landmine. This is easy to miss because it only manifests on the very first increment of the run, so scripts that are usually invoked against fully-compliant inputs (zero issues found) never trigger it in ordinary testing.

When adding a per-phase-scoped required field to a bash validator that currently only does whole-document `grep -qF` existence checks (one match anywhere in the file = pass), do NOT add the field to the whole-document metadata array -- that produces silent under-enforcement where only one of several phases needs to carry the field for the whole check to pass. Instead, locate each phase heading's line number, compute the block range to the next heading (or EOF), and grep only within that range per phase. A required negative fixture (N phases, only some tiered) that expects the exact untiered count as warnings is the way to prove the check is genuinely per-phase and not accidentally still whole-document.
